transcript: Last night I attended the closing performance of The Jungle at Saint Anne Warehouse. It was genuinely one of the most amazing pieces of theater I have ever experienced. The jungle is about a refugee and immigrant camp of the same name that existed in France just 7 years ago. The jungle was once home to more than 8000 people from over a dozen countries. Play follows the experiences of those who have fled their homes and are aiming to seek asylum in France or England. We learn about how and why The Jungle was created, how the people came together to create community and shelter, the stories of those seeking asylum, and the story of The jungle's growth and subsequent demolition by the French government. This play has literally everything I would ever want in a theater piece. It's relevant, deeply moving, impeccably written, directed, designed, and performed, and it creates an experience you can only get through live performance. Production is incredibly immersive, and it really enhances a sense of community among everyone in the room. I am certain this is a piece I will not forget. And if it ever comes back to New York, I will be there. If you're in the DC area, it's going to be there from late March through April 16th, so absolutely go with that. Another program for my collection.
